candidates.core_provocation: In this world, a person can give a memory to someone else—but the giver permanently loses it. On the last day before a colleague leaves the company, she asks him to accept the memory of the one day that made their friendship meaningful, just as they discover that memory is also the key to exposing a serious betrayal.
candidates.why_interesting: Every attempt to preserve the past becomes an act of forgetting, forcing the colleagues to decide whether truth or their shared happiness matters more.

candidates.core_provocation: Whenever three or more people remember the same event differently, reality changes to match the version most people believe. When a colleague is accused of stealing from the company, two coworkers race to recover their own unreliable memories before the team meeting makes the accusation permanently true.
candidates.why_interesting: The characters are not merely arguing about the past—they are fighting to control what actually happened.

candidates.core_provocation: At the end of each workday, everyone forgets one colleague completely, while that colleague remembers everything. A team nearing the end of a difficult project must finish their work and say goodbye to the coworker who is slowly becoming a stranger to all of them.
candidates.why_interesting: The ordinary rituals of office life become a painful countdown, with each forgotten colleague creating both practical danger and emotional loss.

parsed.reason_for_choice: The first idea combines a clear, unusual rule with an immediate emotional dilemma and a concrete secret to uncover. It naturally creates suspense—what is the memory, what betrayal does it reveal, and what will be lost when it is transferred—while keeping the cast, setting, and time frame small.
